title: Contextual bandit threshold autotuner for canary safety guards
creator: Sofia Park
description: Build an automated threshold tuning service that adapts rollback triggers per-customer and per-cohort using a contextual bandit algorithm. Goal is to reduce false-positive rollbacks and decrease time-to-detect true degradations across latency, 5xx error rate, token cost delta, and throughput.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Service runs in canary pipelines and recommends per-cohort thresholds for latency and error-rate within 95% confidence
2) New thresholds applied to canaries reduce unnecessary rollbacks by >= 30% on internal benchmark traffic without increasing exposure time for real degradations
3) All changes are auditable and reversible via existing rollout controller (canary manager), with an immediate override flag
4) Unit and integration tests for bandit learner, thresholds API, and canary enforcement hooks merged to main
5) Dashboard shows recommended threshold, applied threshold, and decision rationale for each canary in the last 14 days
success_metrics: False positive rollback rate decreased by >= 30% on historical test runs
Mean time to rollback for real incidents remains <= current baseline (5m)
No significant increase in customer-facing latency or error-rate attributable to autotuner
Model overhead (CPU/RAM) for bandit service < 5% of canary controller resources
proposed_design: We will implement a contextual bandit that observes feature vectors per canary (baseline SLO percentiles, traffic skew, cohort size, model variant family, time-of-day) and chooses a multiplier on baseline thresholds (e.g., 0.8x..1.5x). Use Thompson Sampling for exploration with decaying prior. Offline simulator will be used to bootstrap priors from historical canary data. The bandit service exposes an HTTP API for: get_recommended_thresholds(canary_id), report_outcome(canary_id, signal_vector, action, reward). The canary controller queries recommendations at canary start and at periodic checkpoints (default 1m). If the live metric exceeds the applied threshold, the existing rollback pipeline is used. All recommended thresholds and decisions are logged to the audit store and surfaced in Console.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal experiments): run bandit in observe-only mode for 2 weeks on staging canaries (no threshold changes applied)
Phase 2 (shadow adjustments): apply recommendations to a small subset of internal customers (1% traffic) with automatic override enabled
Phase 3 (controlled canaries): expand to 10% of canaries with rollback automation enabled but strict guardrails and human-in-the-loop alerts
Phase 4 (general availability): enable for all canaries with opt-out and default safe priors
monitoring_signals: tokens per request and token cost delta vs baseline
cohort size and traffic skew metrics
bandit exploration rate and reward distribution
autotune_strategy: Contextual bandit with Thompson Sampling. Reward is a composite: negative for rollbacks that were not correlated with downstream errors (penalize false positives), large negative for missed degradations, small negative for cost increases above configured budget. Composite reward weights are tunable via feature flags. Offline simulation harness will validate hyperparameters and exploration schedule before production flips.
risk_mitigation: Default conservative prior that biases toward safe (narrow) thresholds
Hard floor/ceiling for thresholds per-metric to prevent extreme adjustments
Immediate supervisor signal: if multiple metrics cross hard SLA limits, force rollback independent of bandit
Canary controller retains manual override and emergency disable flag
Audit logs + automated daily drift report to detect runaway threshold shifts
open_tasks: Design API spec for bandit service and publish to docs (Confluence)
Implement offline simulator and run on last 12 months of canary data
Instrument canary controller to call recommendations API and accept applied_thresholds
Add Console visualization: recommended vs applied vs observed for each metric
Security review for telemetry ingestion and access to canary metadata
Create integration test harness that replays historical canaries and validates no-regression
